B1 is a CORRECT fail against the wrong surface: T-006's acceptance genuinely lacks the word human, but K-5 requires the restatement in REPORT.md's hand-off, and REPORT.md:395 supplies it in a four-column table whose last column reads human. These are the 11th and 12th instrument defects of the run; the standing lesson is unchanged and was again decisive -- a gate is a program and needs its own baseline, not confidence.

decisions.what: Both sealed-gate FAILs (A2, A4) were adjudicated as instrument defects sharing ONE root cause, with the gate left byte-unedited — and a REAL defect the gate never asked about was found by reading.

The repair reads bullets structurally and tests the actor's HEAD clause, with controls in BOTH directions: the stale wording is still rejected, a deleted R-1 bullet is still rejected, an invitation to a builder still FIRES, an agent named in the actor field still FIRES, and an agent assignment HIDDEN inside a parenthetical still FIRES (control K, added specifically to guard the narrowing that made column I pass). Its column J, the control meant to catch exactly that, was a length threshold weak enough to pass on the truncated output; it now requires the structural markers a complete bullet owns. AND THE SHAPE THAT MATTERS MOST, because it is the cycle-14 lesson recurring: the gate was RIGHT AND INSUFFICIENT. Twelve green cells sat over a REPORT.md that told a human to look at 'SPEC.md line 144' for the retag example — the example is at line 206; line 144 is unrelated prose. decisions.what: A conductor cross-check produced a FALSE finding, and it was killed by measuring properly instead of by filing it.

This is the third wrong instrument of the cycle after the gate's own two pre-seal bugs, and the standing lesson holds in a direction worth naming explicitly: the discipline of demanding evidence applies to the CONDUCTOR'S evidence too, and a cross-check that disagrees with a builder is a claim, not a verdict.

It did not change the outcome — the verifier reproduced the finding, found no reviewer overreach, and volunteered the one mitigating fact that argued the severity DOWN from high to medium — and the conductor independently re-derived every decisive fact against the live GitHub API before accepting it. decisions.what: OVERRODE the routing table itself to hold Q-7 at sonnet. This is NOT the gear-2 demotion refusal cycles 1, 4 and 5 recorded — the TABLE routes this item to haiku on its own, before any pacing rule is applied.
decisions.why: reference/workflows.md sends `kind` docs/polish at effort S to haiku, and Q-7 is filed docs/S. But that row states its own intent — "formatting, scaffolding, boilerplate" — and Q-7 is none of those: it writes a new SPEC entry in an existing three-bullet grammar, and reconciles a COUNT claim across REPORT.md by re-deriving it from backlog.json rather than copying a number. Precision about counts and provenance in exactly this document family is the failure mode this repo has now MEASURED four times on haiku agents: run #3 cycle 4 (record N-6) predicted it, run #3 cycle 14 caught a false provenance date written into the one paragraph whose job is dating claims correctly, run #4 cycle 2 caught a builder reporting it wrote "75 lines" for a 22-line file, and cycles 1/4/5 each refused the adjacent demotion on that record. Recorded because it overrides a mechanical rule in the PROMOTE direction under a gear that sets promote=false, which is a stronger override than the three refusals were, and a silent override is how a run starts quietly deciding things it never wrote down. VINDICATED SPECIFICALLY, not merely in outcome: the builder re-derived the count word from backlog.json rather than taking the number from its prompt (gate B6 confirms REPORT and backlog agree), and it reconciled the DEPENDENT claim the prompt only flagged — "documents the last three" -> "the last four" — keeping 2 + 4 = 6 internally consistent. decisions.what: Adjudicated the sealed gate B3/B4 FAILs as INSTRUMENT DEFECTS #19 and #20 with the gate left byte-unedited — and the root cause is one this same gate had ALREADY caught and repaired in itself before sealing.
decisions.why: B3 and B4 read a markdown bullet by taking the first SOURCE LINE matching its label. The builder wrapped its D-45 bullets at ~90 columns while the three pre-existing entries D-42/D-43/D-44 are single unwrapped lines, so "J-7" and "stdout"/"stderr" sat on continuation lines that were structurally out of scope. WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN JUST FIXING: the pre-seal baseline had already found the IDENTICAL defect in cell B5, where the Domain-rules Exit-codes bullet also wraps across two lines and the seal covered only half of it. I repaired B5 and did NOT propagate the repair to the two sibling cells that read bullets the same way. A defect found in one cell of a gate is evidence about every cell of that gate, and I treated it as evidence about one. Adjudicated 8/8 in run4-cycle-008-B3B4-adj.mjs: column A reproduces the miss on the real document, B recovers truth, C proves no regression on the unwrapped format the old reader DID handle, D and E are must-die controls, F and G are MUST-NOT-OVERREACH controls proving the whole-bullet reader cannot absorb a neighbouring bullet — the exact failure mode that produced instrument defects #17/#18 at run #3 cycle 4, so the repair is measured against the bug the repair itself risks introducing. Column H measures the blast radius rather than asserting it: B2 presence regexes scan the whole body and are wrap-immune, so no other cell shares the defect. Both cells failed CLOSED, which is the behaviour you want from a wrong instrument.

decisions.what: The gate own pre-dispatch baseline caught cell A2 passing VACUOUSLY against the unfixed document — a false PASS, not a false FAIL — and A2 was reshaped before sealing.
decisions.why: A2 was a bag-of-words over the whole "## Exit codes" section: stderr AND 3 AND a failure token. Whitespace-normalising that section glues the entire markdown TABLE into one punctuation-free blob, so the sentence splitter produced a single unit carrying tokens harvested from three different rows, and the SHIPPED, UNFIXED row satisfied it — that row names stderr as the DIAGNOSTIC DESTINATION, not as a failing stream. This is the KI-12 / R-1 failure class exactly: a claim satisfied by co-occurrence inside a span no one intended as a sentence. Two repairs, both pre-seal: the unit pool now treats each table row as its OWN unit and never merges neighbours, and A2 was reshaped from a section-wide bag of words into a demand for SUBSTANCE inside the exit-3 row itself. Control C8 was added to pin it — it feeds the sealed cell the literal shipped-unfixed row and requires it to stay dead, so the specific text that fooled A2 can never satisfy it again. THE GENERAL POINT, which is why this is a decision and not a footnote: this run instrument defects have overwhelmingly been false FAILs, which announce themselves. This one was a false PASS, and only a DISCRIMINATING baseline — one that asserts which cells must be RED before the work exists — could have surfaced it. A baseline that merely checked its controls would have shipped it green.

decisions.what: The taste pass returned four findings and this run's locked non-goals forbid acting on essentially all of them — recorded as the cycle's real result rather than buried under the two backlog items it did produce.

Rotation, corpus expansion and 'any new flag' are all LOCKED non-goals of run #4, set by the allocator's trickle brief. F3 is the only one with an in-scope half, and only its DOCUMENTARY half (record the discrepancy; the styling fix itself needs NO_COLOR, also a locked non-goal). So the swarm's independent taste seat, which had never read the kickoff, arrived at the same place the kickoff taste judge did and the same place run #3's cycle-9 taste pass did: the product's ceiling is the corpus and the draw, and this run may not touch either. THIS CORROBORATES THE DISSENT RECORDED IN SPEC.md AT KICKOFF — 'a fourth consecutive run producing zero user-visible value on a repo whose top product improvement (no-repeat rotation) stays deferred suggests the right call is to point the allocator at a different repo.' That dissent was recorded and not overridden because the brief is the operator's to change, not the swarm's, and that remains true: the conductor is not lifting a non-goal for itself. What the conductor CAN do is stop treating the dissent as a kickoff opinion and start treating it as a measured, twice-independently-reproduced finding, and say so in the morning report where the operator will read it.
decisions.consequence: No non-goal lifted. TS-1 and TS-3 gain measured corroboration and stay blocked on the human scope decision. TS-5 filed as todo (the in-scope documentary half of F3). TS-6 filed blocked. The morning report must carry the corroboration prominently: the allocator has now spent four consecutive runs on a repo whose own taste instrument says the remaining value is behind a non-goal wall, and that is an allocator-level decision no cycle of this run can make.

decisions.what: Paid the fable TASTE gate in gear 1 (crawl), which the gear table describes as haiku-priced work.
decisions.why: The budget probe returned gear 1 (rho 4.50, guest mode, weekly ceiling 2, k_cap 1) and gear 1's work-choice guidance is 'haiku-priced useful work ... S-effort sonnet builds only'. A fable judgment agent is the opposite of haiku-priced, so this is an explicit override and is recorded as one rather than slipped through. Three reasons it is the right call. (1) The taste seat is fable-GUARDED: cycle.md and workflows.md both state pacing demotions never demote judgment seats, so the rules do not offer 'run taste on haiku' as an option — the honest choices were pay it at fable or defer it. (2) It is exactly ONE agent, which is the smallest work type in the catalogue and fits gear 1's wave cap of 1 precisely; no cheaper way to discharge this gate exists. (3) The probe put projected window depletion about an hour out, so deferring the last owed gate risked pushing it into a depleted window or a limp episode, with 19.7h of clock still to spend afterwards. Gear 1 governs what a cycle burns, not whether the run's last outstanding gate gets paid.
decisions.consequence: Gate paid. All three pre-POLISH gates are now discharged for run #4 and no further judgment-seat spend is owed this run.

decisions.what: The sealed gate S3 cell FAILED against a working tree that satisfies the scope constraint exactly. INSTRUMENT DEFECT #22, adjudicated 11/11 with the gate left BYTE-UNEDITED.
decisions.why: S3 asks whether README.md is the only changed tracked file. It read `git status --porcelain`, applied .trim() TO THE WHOLE OUTPUT, then sliced 3 characters off each line to skip the two status columns and their separator. But porcelain first column is a SPACE for an unstaged modification (" M README.md"), and the whole-output trim ate it, so the slice started one character late and the cell reported the changed path as "EADME.md". WHY THE PRE-DISPATCH BASELINE DID NOT CATCH IT, which is the part worth carrying: the baseline ran against a CLEAN tree, so porcelain emitted nothing, so no line was ever sliced and the cell passed VACUOUSLY. A discriminating baseline asserts which cells must be RED before the work exists — it did that, correctly, for B1-B4 — but it can still only exercise the code paths the WORLD hands it, and a clean tree hands a status reader no lines at all. That is a new species for this run: the prior defects were cells that were wrong on data they saw; this cell was never given data. It failed CLOSED, which is the right direction. The underlying claim was verified INDEPENDENTLY of the cell: `git status --porcelain | cat -A` by hand returned exactly " M README.md$". Adjudicated in .swarm/runs/run4-c010-S3-adj.mjs with must-die (E), must-not-overreach (F, G) and must-stay-dead (I) columns, plus a blast-radius pair.

decisions.what: The gate was RIGHT AND INSUFFICIENT again, and the gap was found by READING THE DIFF: the delivered README gained a count claim ("24 distinct authors") in the one section that no digit-hygiene guard reaches.
decisions.why: Twenty green cells, every one of them aimed at whether the documentation claim is TRUE, and none at whether it will STAY true. This repo has filed the decay class eight times and has a measured answer to it — run #4 cycle 4 A6 cell, which re-derives every asserted count from its source AT RUN TIME and caught the decay in the act. The Q-6 gate had no such cell because Q-6 acceptance is about a reader understanding, not about a number; the number arrived as a side effect of the builder choosing (correctly, and in this README own voice) to prefer a measured figure to an adjective. MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, and the discriminator matters: this README is unusually well defended against precisely this — test/readme-tags.test.js carries J-5 ("no unrecognised count-claim digits") and C7 ("no digit runs outside the counts table") — but both are SECTION-SCOPED to Tag vocabulary and Attribution, and the new text landed under `## Flags`. The proof that it is genuinely unguarded rather than merely unnamed is that the suite is GREEN at 118/118 with the new "24" in place; had either guard reached that section it would have fired. Filed as Q-8 rather than fixed, because cycle.md step 5 permits ONE work type per cycle — the cycle-2 precedent for evidence obtained inside a build wave.

decisions.what: Corrected Q-6 model from the backlog haiku to sonnet at pick time. This is the routing TABLE being applied, not an override of it — and it is the opposite direction from the three gear-demotion refusals this run recorded.
decisions.why: cycle.md step 4 says routing is PICK-TIME, not plan-time, and workflows.md sends `kind` docs/polish at effort S to haiku while sending "all other build/fix items (S/M effort)" to sonnet. Q-6 is kind=fix, so the table routes it to sonnet and the backlog haiku was a stale PLAN-time assignment. Gear 1 sets demote=true, but the demotion rule drops sonnet to haiku for docs/polish items ONLY, and never lets build/fix fall below sonnet — so pacing does not reach this item either. Recorded because cycles 1, 4 and 5 each recorded a REFUSAL of a haiku demotion on this repo document family, and it would be easy to read this as a fourth. It is not: no rule had to be overridden here, and saying so keeps the three genuine overrides legible as overrides.

decisions.what: Declined to update the eleven stale J-7 behaviour counts in docs/report-history.md while raising the live count from six to seven.
decisions.why: That file is the ARCHIVE of what earlier reports said, moved out of REPORT.md under this run's own M-2 ("history MOVED not deleted"). A count that was true when written is not a defect; rewriting it would falsify the record of what was believed when, which is the one thing an archive exists to prevent. The live count sites — REPORT.md's J-7 bullet and the J-7 backlog record — were both updated in this cycle, and a gate cell pins the archive byte-identical so the decision is enforced rather than merely intended.

decisions.what: Stop instructing builders to build scratch/mutation arms under /tmp. The instruction is unfollowable and this cycle proved it.
decisions.why: The Q-8 builder disclosed that shell cp/mkdir were denied outright for /tmp, so it built its mutation arms INSIDE the repo (.scratch-mutation-test*/) using fs.cpSync instead. The likely cause is structural rather than incidental: /opt/targets/aphorism-cli is an additionalDirectories entry and /tmp is not, so a subagent cannot write there. The agent cleaned up and gate cell S1 came back clean, but the repo has NO .gitignore, so for the duration of the wave a `git add -A` would have committed two full scratch trees. The near-miss was caught only because S1 runs BEFORE the commit. Future builder prompts should name an in-repo scratch path and require its removal, rather than naming a path the sandbox will refuse.

decisions.what: Target DONE. The run definition-of-done was re-derived from the tree by a 12-cell conductor gate (run4-cycle-012-donegate.mjs, 12 PASS / 0 FAIL, 2 must-die controls) rather than trusted from prior cycles. VALUE_LOOP found no candidate clearing the two-question ratchet: every change a user would notice (corpus expansion, no-repeat rotation, a new flag) is a SPEC-locked non-goal for this run, and everything permitted is documentation about documentation - the exact churn M-2 spent this run undoing. Backlog todo 0; all 7 survivors human-owned. ~18.5h left on the clock, handed back with the reason on the record rather than spent. M-3 closes on its handoff branch, never as a pass: the denied script was re-executed this cycle and DENIED again (same run, so the ledger stays at denial #31).

decisions.decision: P-1 closed as BOUNDARY with zero tests added. The suite already executes every REACHABLE branch (64/65); the 65th is dead code. Correcting the kickoff unmeasured 12-of-14 claim to the measured 1-of-7 shrinks this run further and the report will say so rather than pad the clock — remaining weight moves to P-3 and P-4.

decisions.what: Calibrated two cells of the P-3 gate BEFORE dispatch, after its own baseline came back 8 PASS / 3 FAIL with two of the three FAILs being defects in the gate rather than findings about the tree.
decisions.why: The standing lesson of this target is that a gate is a program and needs its own baseline. It fired again, and cheaply, because the baseline ran before any agent did. G1 carried a non-vacuity floor of >=15 citations against a tree that holds 13 — an arbitrary magic number, wrong against reality, lowered to 10. G9 assumed corpus_attribution_triage's #N was a 1-based index; it is 0-based (#0 is Knuth / 'Premature optimization'). The important part is the SHAPE of the second repair: flipping the constant would have made the cell green while leaving it just as blind, so the cell was rewritten to DERIVE the convention from the tree and bind every risk-table row to the corpus entry it names by author AND text prefix. It now reports '0-based binds 50, 1-based binds 0' — a cell that would notice a convention change instead of one that hardcodes today's answer. Pre-dispatch calibration is distinct from editing a gate after it has judged a dispatch, which this run does not do: when the sealed gate later needed a cell it did not have, that cell went into a SEPARATELY-SCORED addendum file and the sealed gate stayed byte-identical to its hash.

decisions.what: Split P-3 so the dispatched half contained NO judgment: the agent enumerated and measured prose claims read-only and wrote exactly one untracked file, and the conductor adjudicated every verdict and made every correction.
decisions.why: Gear 1 crawl (rho 3.61, weekly governor hot at ceiling 2, k_cap 1) routes an M-effort docs item to haiku by the demote rung — and this target has a cycle-numbered precedent (cycle-4 N-6) of haiku overclaiming on exactly this document family. The available dodges were both bad: flagging the item route_class core to reach fable would have been the conductor gaming its own pacing system in a trickle-posture run, and skipping the item would have left a spec must-have unclosed. The third option is to change what is dispatched rather than who receives it. Enumeration across four surfaces is labour, not judgment; deciding whether a claim is true is judgment. So the agent got the labour with a hard read-only fence and an explicit instruction that UNVERIFIED is a respected answer and an invented measurement is the worst possible one, and every verdict it returned was re-measured here. The precedent held anyway — its summary claimed 71 TRUE against 58 TRUE rows in its own table — but it landed as a bookkeeping error in an untracked scratch file, caught by counting rather than believing, instead of as a false claim shipped into README.md.

decisions.what: Excluded REPORT.md and docs/report-history.md from the P-3 audit surface, and said so before auditing rather than after.
decisions.why: P-3's acceptance names 'README, --help output and docs/'. Taken literally that includes docs/report-history.md, which is 128 KB and 1595 lines of APPEND-ONLY history — dated statements of what was believed at a past cycle, structurally the same artifact as the journal. Auditing those against today's tree is a category error: they are not claims about now, and 'correcting' them would destroy the record of what was believed when, which is the same argument cycle 2 made when it recorded a falsified claim in a new block instead of editing the cycle-1 block that contained it. REPORT.md is excluded on a different ground: it is a live document, but it carries its own cycle-14 gate and WRAP_UP rewrites it, so auditing it now audits a draft. That leaves 567 lines of live claim surface across four documents, which is what was actually audited — a scope decision recorded here so the report cannot read as if 'docs/' had been swept whole.

decisions.what: The sealed gate was RIGHT AND SUFFICIENT, and caught a self-falsifying property BEFORE the commit landed. First time on this repo that an instrument pre-empted the decay class instead of recording it after a human read the diff.
decisions.why: P-6 mechanizes README Node-support own quoted falsifier — `git diff <base>..HEAD -- src bin test .github`. The new test lives under test/, INSIDE that pathspec, so committing it makes the cited diff non-empty and the guard falsifies the citation it guards. The gate returned 7/9 with A3 and A7 red on that single root cause (A7 being the same cause surfacing in a second cell — the cells agreeing, not two defects), and I verified it independently of the cells with `git log --oneline -1 --name-only 0c2ed40` before acting. WHAT MAKES THE SHAPE NEW: eleven prior recorded outcomes on this repo were the instrument being WRONG, and two (cycle 14, run #4 cycle 4) were the gate being RIGHT AND INSUFFICIENT — twelve green cells over a document containing a falsehood none was aimed at, found by reading afterwards. This one was aimed at the right thing and fired before any commit existed. NOT RESOLVED BY WEAKENING: narrowing the pathspec or softening the assertion would each have been deleting a claim, which this run non-goals forbid. Resolved by the CI round trip the section itself prescribes — commit the test, push, read the archived log of run 32328776838, re-cite to it. The four jobs each reported 120 tests / 119 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped, and that identical skip is real-world confirmation of the shallow-clone arm on all four Node majors, which is stronger evidence than the local depth-1 clone and settles the builder own UNVERIFIED caveat about Node 18/20/22.

decisions.what: Recorded a genuine P-5 EXCEPTION rather than re-labelling it, and filed the invariant conflict as P-7 for a human instead of resolving it.
decisions.why: P-5 requires the suite green at >=119 on EVERY commit this run makes. Commit 5f833ab is RED on a full clone. It is green in CI (depth-1 checkout makes the cited base unreachable, so the guard skips) and c0337f1 restores full-clone green one commit later, but the intermediate commit genuinely does not meet the floor. THE WINDOW IS INTRINSIC, NOT A DEFECT: any commit touching src/bin/test/.github falsifies the citation the instant it lands, and the CI run that refreshes the citation cannot exist before the push. I considered and rejected three dodges — anchoring the citation to a branch/tag commit outside master history (unreadable for a document whose whole job is being checkable by a human), narrowing the pathspec (test/ genuinely belongs in it: adding a test changes the count the cited table asserts), and softening the assertion (deleting a claim). Every remaining disposition amends a locked SPEC must-have or retires a shipped guard, and this run non-goals forbid the swarm doing either for itself. So the honest move is to state the exception plainly, in the commit message, the transcript, the README and the report, and hand the ruling to the operator. Re-defining the floor to make a red commit read as green is the exact failure mode hard rule 2 forbids.

decisions.what: Ran REVIEW-FIX instead of the DONE decision cycle 5 handed forward, and pointed stage 2 at the reviewer’s CLEAN VERDICT rather than at findings, because there were none.
decisions.why: ON THE WORK TYPE: cycle 5’s hand-off asked cycle 6 to run VALUE_LOOP/DONE. cycle.md step 4 outranks a prior cycle’s suggestion — it places ONE review-fix, ONE QA and ONE TASTE pass after BUILD and before POLISH, and run #5 had run NONE of the three. This is the identical call run #4 cycle 5 made, for the identical reason, and the trap it avoids is one this repo has already paid for: run #3 cycle 8 declared DONE and was wrong four times over, every error tracing to a mandatory gate that had never run while the bookkeeping said it had. The qa markers in this object (last_full_qa_cycle 7, last_taste_cycle 9) are RUN #3 numbers carried forward; this cycle added run-scoped keys so a later cycle cannot misread them. ON THE STAGE-2 ADAPTATION, which is the part worth recording: the review-fix contract sends stage-1 findings to adversarial verifiers that must REPRODUCE them, discarding what cannot be reproduced. Stage 1 returned ZERO findings, so that pipeline had nothing to consume and the pass would have closed as clean. But the reviewer had been demoted from its table seat (opus) to sonnet by gear 1, and a cheap reviewer’s characteristic failure is not a wrong finding — it is SILENCE, which from outside is indistinguishable from a clean surface. So the fable verifier was aimed at the clean verdict itself, with the reviewer’s five specific claims restated as attack targets and an explicit instruction that UPHELD requires describing what was mutated. It refuted three of the five. Had stage 2 been skipped for want of findings, all three would have shipped under the label “reviewed clean”.
decisions.consequence: Three findings, every one reproduced independently by the conductor before anything changed. RF-1 fixed by dispatch under a sealed gate (10 PASS / 0 FAIL); RF-2 and RF-3 by conductor repair. RF-4 filed from a CI annotation, not fixed. QA-full and TASTE are still owed by run #5.

decisions.what: The sealed gate scored 10/10 immediately after the fix, then 8/10 when re-run later against a byte-identical fix. Both later FAILs are cells run OUTSIDE the window they were authored to score. Adjudicated, with the gate left BYTE-UNEDITED at sha256 9d3743cb.
decisions.why: B9 asks whether the only changed tracked path outside .swarm/ is the guard file — i.e. whether the FIXER edited README.md to make the guard agree with it. That question is about the dispatch window, and by the re-run the window had closed: the fix was committed at c08562b and README.md was dirty because the CONDUCTOR was performing the re-citation round trip the section itself prescribes. The cell measured the right property at the wrong moment. It is answered decisively and independently of the cell by the commit: c08562b touches .github/workflows/test.yml, docs/coverage-baseline.md, test/node-support-citation.test.js and two .swarm artifacts, and README.md is ABSENT from it. B6 requires that a genuine depth-1 clone still SKIP — the must-not-overreach control protecting the CI path. It returned PASS, and that is a TRUE reading of a transient state rather than a regression: mid-round-trip the working tree cited c08562b while HEAD WAS c08562b, so the cited base was present even in a depth-1 clone and the guard could evaluate it for once. RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY ARGUMENT: the re-citation was committed, HEAD moved past the cited base, and the gate re-run returned B6 to SKIP. WHY THIS IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT DEFECT, which matters because this repo has filed 23 of those and the count should stay honest: neither cell was wrong about the world — both reported accurately, and what moved underneath them was which moment they sampled. The lesson is narrower and newer than the standing one that a gate is a program needing its own baseline: a gate cell has a VALID WINDOW as well as a correct assertion, and a cell whose subject is an agent dispatch stops being meaningful the moment the conductor itself starts editing.

decisions.what: Deferred the owed TASTE gate one cycle and spent the cycle on RF-4 instead.
decisions.why: TASTE is the last of the three passes cycle.md makes mandatory before POLISH and cycle 7 named it as next, so this is a deliberate deferral rather than an oversight. Two independent grounds. GEAR: at gear 1 the work-choice rule is haiku-priced work with S-effort sonnet builds only, and a taste pass is one FABLE agent — a judgment seat, correctly exempt from demotion, and therefore the single most expensive dispatch available — at rho 7.92 with the weekly governor pinned at ceiling 2. MARGINAL VALUE, which is the stronger reason: taste findings route to feature and polish items, this run's allocator brief forbids new features outright, and the depth findings a taste agent would surface on a 50-entry corpus are ALREADY on the board and already blocked by that same brief — TS-1 (repeats by the ~9th draw), TS-2 (five tag pools <= 4 entries), TS-3 (three voices hold a third of the corpus), TS-6 (undiscoverable tag vocabulary). Paying a fable seat to re-file items the run may not act on is ceremony. The gate is owed before POLISH, not before every cycle, and ~20h of clock remain.

decisions.what: Adjudicated the sealed gate's A4 FAIL as instrument defect #15 and repaired it in a SEPARATE artifact, leaving the gate byte-unedited.
decisions.why: A4 guarded against a coverage THRESHOLD flag with a regex over the whole workflow file, and matched test.yml:36 — a COMMENT that names those flags in order to forbid them. It read the prohibition as the violation. Settled by two facts independent of judgement: grep localises every hit to comment lines or to the different --experimental-test-coverage flag, and git show 057d00c of the same path contains the identical string, so the builder could not have introduced it. It failed CLOSED (accused a clean file), unlike run #3 cycle 15 S1 which under-measured and still exited 0. Repaired additively per the standing precedent from run #3 cycles 4/12/14 and run #4 cycle 1 — rewriting a gate after it has run destroys the evidence of what it measured — with a six-column measurement proving the old predicate still misfires, the new one clears the real file, the new one STILL catches a real threshold flag in a run: step, ignores one in a comment, recomposes A4 to PASS, and goes red when the glob-assert step is deleted. The sharp part is worth keeping: this run ships a standing QA prompt line reading "Never assert against prose matched by regex", and the conductor is what broke it.

decisions.what: Did NOT credit wave autotune despite the build item passing its gate.
decisions.why: Unlike cycles 6 and 7 the work type WAS a build item, so autotune is in scope. But the rule requires CLEAN = zero reverts AND zero failed verifies, and the gate emitted one FAIL that took a conductor adjudication to clear. Adjudicated-clean is not clean, and crediting it would raise k_current to 4 while gear 1 pins k_cap at 1 — buying nothing this run but a wrong number on the board, which is the argument cycle 6 recorded when it declined the same credit for a different reason.
